findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted at rest by default, risking exposure of potentially sensitive report data.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No acl attribute is set and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource for this bucket, leaving it reliant on account-level defaults for public access restriction rather than an explicit private configuration, increasing risk of unintended exposure.
The bucket stores ledger export data (likely sensitive financial data) but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket storing model artifacts, so data is unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so operational runbook content (potentially containing sensitive operational details) is stored unencrypted at rest.

The object is uploaded to reports_archive, a bucket without server-side encryption configured, and the object itself does not specify a kms_key_id or server_side_encryption override, so this potentially sensitive vendor roster file is stored in cleartext at rest.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be destroyed without protection, and combined with the absence of versioning this could enable irrecoverable data loss, including as a result of compromised credentials or erroneous automation.
